## The Prompt

I want to write a C++23 and a python program that take an ISBN/DOI code and generate the BibTeX code.
The 2 programs must implement the following requirements:

1. It must be a CLI program with the following syntax: isbn2bibtex [ --help ] [ --version ] [ --log \<log-file> ] { \<isbn-or-doi> | --read-from-file \<isbn-or-doi-file-name> } [ --save-to-file \<bibtex-file-name> ] [ --retry \<max-retries> [--delay \<seconds> ] ]
2. \<isbn-or-doi> is either a single or double-quoted string providing either an ISBN or a DOI code;
3. \<isbn-or-doi-file-name> contains a list of ISBN/DOI codes, one per line; no single or double quotes are needed in the file. Blank lines, lines starting with or any text following a `#` must be ignored;
4. only one of the two command line arguments, \<isbn-or-doi> or \<isbn-or-doi-file-name>, must be provided;
5. ISBN check digits must be validated, and ISBN-10 should be converted to ISBN-13;
6. The program must also accept `doi:`, `https://doi.org/` and `ISBN-13:` prefixes;
7. if provided, \<bibtex-file-name> is the file where all BibTeX codes generated are stored in append mode; the file is created if missing; the file name must have extension `.bib`, if not the program must add it automatically warning the user of this change;
8. all BibTeX codes generated must be copied to clipboard so that at the end of the program they can be copied somewhere; the copy to clipboard must be done even if they have been saved to a file as specified by the flag --save-to-file;
9. internet connection must be available to fetch the data related to the ISBN/DOI codes; the program must terminate with a failure message if no internet connection is up and running;
10. a log file must be written and is located at the working directory where the app is launched; log files must have extension `.log`; if the optional command line argument --log is provided use \<log-file> as log file, otherwise use a default name; if \<isbn-or-doi-file-name> is provided, the default name must be built from \<isbn-or-doi-file-name> with extension `.log`;
11. every time an ISBN/DOI code generates a BibTeX code a log file must be updated adding a line so made: '\<ISBN-or-DOI-code>: BibTeX generated with request: \<HTTP-request>'; the same line must be emitted on terminal; \<HTTP-request> must log the HTTP request that succeeded; the BibTeX structure must contain at least: `author`, `title`, `publisher`, `address`, `year`, `url`, `isbn`;
12. every time a BibTeX code cannot be generated for an ISBN/DOI code a log file must be updated adding a line so made: '\<ISBN-or-DOI-code>: FAILED: \<reason-of-failure>'; the same line must be emitted on terminal; \<reason-of-failure> must contain the HTTP request(s) that failed; if an HTTP error code is reported, then print the human-readable textual description for it;
13. only for HTTP codes 408, 429 the optional command line argument --retry specifies the max number of attempts for retrying a failed request; \<max-retries> defaults to 0 if not provided; the optional command line argument --delay is considered only if --retry is provided and it is a real number for seconds to wait before retrying a new HTPP request; \<seconds> defaults to 0.5 if not provided; the log line should mention which attempt was tried after the first failure;
14. The log, `.bib` and input files must be three different files;
15. Optional command line argument --help must print a help text about the usage of the tool;
16. Optional command line argument --version must print the version of the tool;
17. For the C++23 implementation: Provide a `Makefile` for compiling the C++23 program so that it runs on linux ubuntu 24.04 or later; do not to generate code for other platforms or operating systems. In the `Makefile` also implement: `makes strip`; `make clean`; `make install`; `make uninstall`; `make help`. The compilation outputs and binaries must be saved in a build directory, e.g. `build/`. The binary executable must be installed in the default place for linux ubuntu, if not specified otherwise;
18.
